types.description: Registry anchor for the declared API surface (ADR-0030, ADR-0054): not authorable. The `api` subtype axis is the interaction model, never the protocol; protocol lives in `binding.*` on each operation.

A named, packaged request/response surface whose children are operations (ADR-0030). It is a wire contract: two of them (`v1`, `v2`) may declare the same operation side by side. The code behind it is one service per metadata package, whose surface is the package's operations (ADR-0064).
types.whenToUse: The application does something beyond derived CRUD: a named command (approve, cancel, import) or a named query (my open requests). Declare it here so its input, output, permission and business errors are part of the model. A plain lifecycle needs no api.operational at all: each transition nobody claims derives its own command.
types.rules: Children are `operation.command` and `operation.query`. Lives at the document root. Declares no fields, sources or identities: shapes are referenced, never defined, by the surface.

types.description: Registry anchor for the attributes every operation shares (ADR-0054): not authorable.

children.description: Optional protocol bindings. Only needed to override the derived method and path.

children.name: inputRef
children.description: The `object.value` this operation takes as its input (ADR-0030). Absent on an operation whose only parameter is the target's borrowed key. Anything other than an `object.value` is ERR_OPERATION_SHAPE.

children.name: outputRef
children.description: The object this operation returns: an `object.projection`, `object.entity` or `object.value`. Which projection a query returns is the author's choice among several over one entity, so it cannot be computed. Anything else is ERR_OPERATION_SHAPE.

children.name: objectRef
children.description: The entity this operation acts on, declared only when it cannot be derived. It is derived from the input value's field that `extends` the entity's primary key field, else from the output's base entity. Declared and derivable, the two must agree (ERR_OPERATION_TARGET_MISMATCH). It must name an `object.entity` (ERR_OPERATION_TARGET_UNRESOLVED).

children.name: permission
children.description: The permission name the generated shell asks the project's policy about before anything is written. A key into grant data (who holds it is data, what the policy decides is code), so it is never derived from the operation's name: a rename would silently move access. Absent and not @public: the shell uses the derived name `<package>.<operation>`, and `verify` advises or requires an explicit one (setting `rules.permissions.names`). Several operations may share one.

children.name: public
children.description: The shell calls no permission check. Authentication is the transport's job and is unaffected. Absent means checked. Declaring it with @permission is ERR_PERMISSION_PUBLIC_CONFLICT.

types.description: A named operation that changes state. Takes an `object.value` (ADR-0030). Its body is hand-written; the generated shell around it loads the row, checks the permission and the current state, runs the body, and makes the guarded update in one transaction (ADR-0063).
types.whenToUse: A business action with its own name, input and rules: approve, cancel, transfer. A command that moves a lifecycle names the transitions it may make in @transitions; its body decides which one applies.

children.name: transitions
children.description: The lifecycle moves this command may make: names of `transition.action` nodes on its target entity (ERR_OPERATION_UNKNOWN_TRANSITION otherwise). A fact of the business the model cannot compute. A transition a command lists gets no derived command of its own. Listing any requires a target (ERR_OPERATION_TARGET_UNRESOLVED).

children.name: errors
children.description: The business failures the hand-written body may return, each a lower snake case code (`insufficient_funds`). They name the wire error, the OpenAPI document and the typed result; the shell refuses an undeclared one. A code that is not lower snake case, or appears twice, is ERR_BAD_ATTR_VALUE.

types.description: A named operation that reads. Returns an `object.projection` (or an entity or value). It changes nothing.
types.whenToUse: A read with its own name and shape beyond derived get and list: my open requests, the dashboard summary.

children.name: many
children.description: The query returns a list and takes the filter, sort and paging contract. Not implied by the projection, so declared. Absent means one row. Legal on a query only.

types.description: Registry anchor for protocol bindings (ADR-0030, ADR-0054): not authorable.

The HTTP method and path of an operation, declared only to override the derived ones. A query is `GET`, a command `POST`; the path is `/<collection>/{id}/<operation-kebab>` for an operation with a target key and `/<collection>/<operation-kebab>` without one (setting `api.operationPaths` chooses the `:verb` style). Most models never write it.
types.whenToUse: An operation must keep a method or path the derived one would not give it, such as an existing public URL.

children.name: method
children.description: The HTTP method. Absent: GET for a query, POST for a command.

children.name: path
children.description: A path template. Its `{name}` placeholders must be exactly the target's primary key fields when the operation is keyed, and there must be none when it is not (ERR_BINDING_PATH_MISMATCH).
